clue.text: Majority of stuff in joker's comeback gets a laugh

indicators.note: the shortened word for stuff goes inside the turned word
a comeback turns the joker's word round so it runs backwards

parts.note: a wag is a joker

indicators.note: most of the word, all but its first letter, is kept

parts.note: guff is stuff in the sense of nonsense or empty talk

explanation.surface: A comedian's clever retort full of nonsense raises a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority of' keeps three of the four letters, 'comeback' turns the joker word round, and 'in' places one inside the other. Stuff means nonsense here, not material.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud hearty burst of laughter is what someone gets when the room roars.

clue.text: I start to gulp sticky things on top of fruit

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sitting on top of another comes before it

parts.note: goos are gooey, sticky substances
the ego is the self, the I

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word gulp is used

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down fruit that has sticky stuff on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top of' in a down clue puts the sticky things above the rest. GOOSEGOG is British dialect for a gooseberry; 'I' as the self is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosegog is an informal British name for the gooseberry, a sour green berry.

clue.text: … having a portion right away during a party

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is sent away, removed from the word for portion

parts.note: a fraction is a portion or part

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone takes a share right away at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots link the surface to the clue before; 'away' drops R from FRACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting group or clique within a larger political body.

clue.text: No, I'd interrupt a lot, sounding very nasal

indicators.note: the words 'No, I'd' break into the phrase for a lot, sitting in its middle

parts.note: a deal, as in 'a great deal', means a lot
taken as written, the letters of no and I'd

explanation.surface: Someone protests 'No, I'd...' while constantly interrupting in a nasal whine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupt' places the words 'No, I'd' in the middle of the phrase for a lot, so the surface's chatty protest is really fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged adenoids block the nose and give speech a stuffy, blocked tone.

clue.text: I'll see New York, shortly, recollecting paths once trod

indicators.note: recollecting suggests gathering and re-collecting, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
NY is the short form of New York

explanation.surface: A traveller promises to visit New York briefly while remembering old trails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollecting' shuffles ILLSEE plus NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ley lines are supposed ancient straight tracks linking prehistoric sites across the landscape.

clue.text: Point improved a talk organised for dairy product

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone sharpened a point and improved a lecture about a dairy product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the three words after Point; the compass letter is set in front, not shuffled in.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick canned milk has had much of its water removed by heating.

clue.text: Source of gold in rich vein accounts for the cabin

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for the vein

parts.note: a lode is a vein of metal ore in rock

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Gold found in a rich seam pays for a log cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts G inside LODE; 'accounts for the' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house or hut, such as a hunting or gatekeeper's lodging.

clue.text: A small compartment in rear portion of plane?

definitions.text: A small compartment in rear portion of plane?

indicators.note: the A and the cell go inside the trimmed word
only the back end of the word plane, its last two letters, is kept

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a cell is a small compartment or room

explanation.surface: A question about a small compartment at the back of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear portion of' keeps the last two letters of the aircraft word; 'in' houses the compartment inside them. The whole clue also describes an engine housing, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is a streamlined housing on an aircraft, holding an engine, crew or cargo.

clue.text: Give short measure on one's sea food?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another comes above it

parts.note: to scamp is to skimp, giving less than is due
the Roman numeral I is one; the 's is linking

explanation.surface: A fishmonger cheats customers by short-weighting the seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts SCAMP above I.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are large prawns, Norway lobsters, usually served fried in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Nick's heard enthusing about English printing method

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for nick is what is said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: to nick is to steal in British slang
raving about something is enthusing about it

explanation.surface: Nick is overheard raving about English printing techniques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives the sound-alike of the nick word; the raving is about English, so that abbreviation is set first. Nick is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a process in which designs cut into metal plates are inked and pressed onto paper.

clue.text: Band of gold depicted on breast by artist?

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
the chest is the breast
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A gold necklace is painted lying on a sitter's chest by a portraitist.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword staple for artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Yes. Russian tea may be found in this cottage

parts.note: da is the Russian word for yes
cha (char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A Russian agrees that tea is served in this country house.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or summer villa.

clue.text: I'll be in record book as a prime example

indicators.note: I will be in, sitting inside the record and book words

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a tome is a large book
the letter I, as the subject of 'will be in'

explanation.surface: A boast: I will appear in the record books as the finest example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be in' says the I sits inside the record-plus-book pair; the surface's boast about record books is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect representative of a type or quality.

clue.text: Performances of bowler and miler have something in common

parts.note: in cricket an over is a bowler's spell of six balls
a lap is one circuit run by a middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: A cricketer and an athlete find their efforts share something.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a cricket term: a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that coincide in part, sharing some ground, are said to overlap.

clue.text: Had nothing new brought in to get married?

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: these letters are brought inside the word for married

parts.note: to wed is to marry; wed is also the past form

explanation.surface: Someone poor with nothing new had to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts ON inside WED.
explanation.definitionFit: Owned means possessed, a sense of 'had'.

clue.text: He may scan the papers with passing interest

definitions.text: He may scan the papers with passing interest

parts.words: He may scan the papers with passing interest
parts.note: not a newspaper reader but a candidate reading exam papers, keen to pass

explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting a test reads question papers hoping to pass.

clue.text: Bury forward has to fit in with the rest

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a lock is a forward position in rugby

explanation.surface: A football club from Bury needs a forward who fits in with the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also an English town with a football club; here it is the verb. In rugby, the lock is a second-row forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts that interlock engage with each other, as gears or jigsaw pieces do.

clue.text: Modified gun inlay is rather clumsy

indicators.note: the letters are modified into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gun's ornamental inlay, once altered, looks awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modified' rearranges GUNINLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungainly describes awkward, graceless movement or appearance.

clue.text: Good golfer's record mentioned in introduction

indicators.note: mentioned means the phrase is spoken, so it is matched by sound

parts.note: a pro is a good golfer; a log is a record

explanation.surface: A top golfer's scorecard gets a mention in the opening remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' says PRO LOG is said aloud, giving the word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is the opening section of a play or book.

clue.text: The right colour for linen — it's possibly fresher

parts.note: ecru is the beige colour of unbleached linen
taken as written, the 's is linking

explanation.surface: A remark about the proper shade for linen being fresher.
explanation.walkthrough: A fresher is a British first-year university student: a new arrival, like a recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruit is a newcomer to an organisation, as a first-year student is.

clue.text: I may be put in a shift in the city …

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the word for a shift

parts.note: a turn is a shift, as in a stint of work

explanation.surface: Someone muses about being put on a shift in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be put in' places I inside TURN. The leading dots run on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in north-west Italy.

clue.text: Don, perhaps, has taken in note for ship-builder

indicators.note: the river word takes the note inside it

parts.note: the Don is a river, in Russia or England
te is a note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A university don has taken notes on shipbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: Don looks like a lecturer but is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A riveter fastens metal plates with rivets, as in hull construction.

clue.text: Nothing's to be kept in an apartment aboard ship

indicators.note: the letter is kept inside the phrase for an apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
O is zero, nothing; the 's is linking

explanation.surface: Nothing may be stored in a cramped flat on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be kept in' places O inside A FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Afloat means at sea, on board a vessel.

clue.text: … if such a processing plant appears

indicators.note: the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: if such a factory appears in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processing' rearranges IFSUCHA. Plant misleads as a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuchsia is a shrub with drooping purple and red flowers.

clue.text: It takes a smart man to expand ocean development

definitions.meaning: a dandy or toff, someone stylish
a heaving rise of the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a swell; to grow is to swell; a long rolling wave is a swell.

clue.text: Excellent "No. 5" scent almost rejected in Czech region

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written with I for 1
V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an aroma is a scent

explanation.surface: A famous perfume, Chanel No. 5, is turned down in a Czech province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims AROMA to AROM; 'rejected' reverses A1 + V + AROM, all together.
explanation.definitionFit: Moravia is the eastern historical land of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Egg's container said to be appropriate to the festive season

indicators.note: said means the phrase is spoken, matched by sound

parts.note: of Yule, belonging to Christmas

explanation.surface: A remark that eggs suit Christmas time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives the word that sounds like OF YULE.
explanation.definitionFit: In plants, the ovule is the structure holding the egg cell, becoming the seed.

clue.text: I'll try getting back a kind of profit made dishonestly

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a go is a try

indicators.note: getting back means the profit word is read backwards

parts.note: nett profit is one kind

explanation.surface: A trader vows to recover a profit gained by fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back' reverses NETT to TTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten gains were acquired by illegal or unethical means.

clue.text: Training in France, you may get note about Mistral's return

parts.note: tu is French for you

indicators.note: the note goes about, around, the reversed wind word

parts.note: te is a note in sol-fa

indicators.note: return means the wind word is read backwards

parts.note: the mistral is a strong wind, a gale, in southern France

explanation.surface: Instruction in France comes with a note on the poet Mistral's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the wind word and 'about' wraps the note round it. Mistral misleads as the Provencal poet; it is the strong cold wind of southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or guardianship given by a tutor.

clue.text: Small island, a Scots one, almost suppresses sin

indicators.note: the shortened island holds the word for sin down inside it
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A small Scottish island nearly keeps sin under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the island's last letter and 'suppresses' holds the sin word inside. Skye is a large island off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a rocky islet or reef, especially off Scotland.
